name: Vishaka v State of Rajasthan
holding: The Court laid down workplace sexual harassment guidelines pending legislation.

name: Aureliano Fernandes v State of Goa
holding: Workplace inquiries must respect procedural fairness.

name: D.K. Basu v State of West Bengal
holding: The Court prescribed safeguards for arrest and detention.

name: Lalita Kumari v Government of Uttar Pradesh
holding: Under the then CrPC, information disclosing a cognizable offence required FIR registration.

name: Arnesh Kumar v State of Bihar
holding: Arrest must be justified under the applicable statutory criteria.

name: Rangappa v Sri Mohan
holding: The statutory presumption extends to a legally enforceable debt and can be rebutted.

name: Basalingappa v Mudibasappa
holding: An accused can rebut the presumption on a preponderance of probabilities.

name: C.C. Alavi Haji v Palapetty Muhammed
holding: Properly addressed postal notice can attract a presumption of service.

name: Rajnesh v Neha
holding: Financial disclosure assists maintenance decisions and courts should consider overlapping awards.

name: Shamim Ara v State of U.P.
holding: A bare assertion of an earlier talaq did not establish a valid divorce.

name: Shayara Bano v Union of India
holding: A majority set aside instant triple talaq.

name: Vineeta Sharma v Rakesh Sharma
holding: Daughters acquire coparcenary rights by birth under the amended Hindu Succession Act.

name: Suraj Lamp & Industries v State of Haryana
holding: A general power of attorney sale does not by itself convey title.

name: Kale v Deputy Director of Consolidation
holding: Bona fide family arrangements can bind the parties subject to applicable formalities.

name: Lucknow Development Authority v M.K. Gupta
holding: Housing construction by a development authority may be a consumer service.

name: Indian Medical Association v V.P. Shantha
holding: The Court addressed when medical services fell within the 1986 consumer statute.

name: National Seeds Corporation v M. Madhusudhan Reddy
holding: An arbitration clause did not bar the statutory consumer remedy.

name: Emaar MGF Land v Aftab Singh
holding: An arbitration agreement did not oust the consumer forum.

name: Dharangadhara Chemical Works v State of Saurashtra
holding: Supervision and control help distinguish employment from independent contracting.

name: Bangalore Water Supply v A. Rajappa
holding: The Court interpreted industry broadly under the Industrial Disputes Act.

name: People’s Union for Democratic Rights v Union of India
holding: Payment below minimum wages can amount to forced labour.

name: CBSE v Aditya Bandopadhyay
holding: Evaluated answer books are information accessible under RTI subject to statutory limits.

name: Girish Ramchandra Deshpande v Central Information Commissioner
holding: The Court applied the then personal-information exemption to employee records.

name: K.S. Puttaswamy v Union of India
holding: Privacy is a fundamental right protected by the Constitution.

name: Shreya Singhal v Union of India
holding: Section 66A of the Information Technology Act was struck down.
